title: SAML federation and customer key handoff acceptance plan
creator: Ethan Rodriguez
description: This ticket captures the product acceptance plan for tenant-level SAML federation (SP and IdP onboarding), RBAC role mapping for federated users, and the operational handoff for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in Private deployments. The goal is to define clear, testable acceptance criteria and a sign-off checklist for legal/compliance, security, and customer success before GA. Scope includes SCIM/JIT provisioning decisions for identity, SAML assertion mapping, KMS key wrapping and rotation, HSM attestation, and audit log retention/forwarding requirements.
acceptance_criteria: SAML: SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows validated with three major IdPs (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace) using test tenants and documented SAML metadata exchange process.
Assertion mapping: SAML attributes map to RBAC roles with automated mapping test suites covering at least 10 role permutations and failing safely to a least-privilege default.

Provisioning: If SCIM is enabled, user creation/deprovisioning must occur within 60s of IdP event (measured in staging). If SCIM is not available, documented manual onboarding runbook exists and is tested end-to-end.
KMS/HSM: Customer key import and envelope encryption flow validated end-to-end using HSM-backed keys; key wrapping/unwrapping latency under 50ms for 95th percentile in dedicated infra tests.
Key lifecycle: Automated rotation policy exercised in staging with a documented rollback plan; rotation must not interrupt live inference traffic; test contains a rotation & rollback run.

Audit logs: All identity, key management, and admin actions produce immutable audit events with schema documented; logs are shipped to customer SIEM and retained for 365 days by default with configurable retention.
Access controls: Console and API role matrix implemented; tests ensure API keys scoped to tenant-level roles cannot access other tenants' resources.
Compliance checklist: Security, Legal, and Customer Success have signed acceptance for production onboarding, with evidence links attached (PRs, test runs, and runbooks).
Observability: Console shows token-level cost/latency for requests using customer keys; incidents related to key errors generate alert and tracing breadcrumbs for triage.
Performance: No more than 5% tail latency increase attributable to KMS/HSM envelope operations when enabled compared to unencrypted baseline in equivalent infra.
Packaging: Private deployment artifacts (installer, helm/chart, or AMI) document KMS key injection points, HSM attestation steps, and necessary network ACLs for IdP endpoints.
Documentation: PRD, onboarding runbook, and customer-facing checklist published; internal runbook includes escalation matrix and contingency contacts.
signoff_checklist: Security Reviewer (Claire Patel) has validated threat model and approved mitigations for SAML assertion spoofing and key access.
Compliance (Jordan Li) confirmed audit schema and retention meets primary customer/regulatory requirements.
Operations (Diego Alvarez) completed a staged onboarding with synthetic traffic and confirmed no data leakage and acceptable latency.
Customer Success (Priya Kapoor) performed a pilot onboarding with one reference customer and recorded onboarding feedback.
Engineering (runtime & infra owners) signed off on performance tests and provided PR links for SCIM/SAML/KMS changes.
Legal approved customer KMS contract language and responsibilities in the onboarding checklist.
Product (owner) confirms all acceptance criteria passed and attaches evidence artifacts to this ticket.
scope_changes: 2025-03-04: Initial scope included optional SCIM for all customers. Decision: SCIM will be MVP for enterprise tier only; manual onboarding runbook remains for others. Rationale: limited engineering capacity and priority of HSM integration.
2025-03-07: Delayed support for non-envelope KMS patterns (bring-your-own-unencrypted-keys) to a follow-up ticket. Reason: security review required additional controls.
2025-03-10: Added explicit HSM attestation requirement after SOC team raised concerns about key provenance during air-gapped installs.
2025-03-11: Reduced default audit retention from 3 years to 365 days with configurable option; legal accepted as lower baseline for GA with add-on available.
